Here we visualise the finprint data and then start developing a Bayesian hierarchical model to estimate causal effects of conservation.

#### Fishing restrictions model

We focus on building the **Fishing restrictions model** first. To estimate the causal effect of fishing restrictions on reef shark abundance we need to include the following reef level covariates: shark fishing restrictions, MPA presence; and the following national level covariates: Human development index (HDI), Governance effectiveness (GOV), Voice and accountability (VOICE), and shark sanctuary presence (SSA); as informed by the following structural causal model directed acyclic graph (DAG; Klinard et al. *in prep*):

![Causal factors influencing reef shark abundance globally](images/dag.png)

##### Wrangle and visualise the data

```{r}
#| output: false
#| warning: false
# read in, wrangle and visualise the data
library(tidyverse) 
library(GGally)

#dat <- read.csv('data/fpdat_final.csv') |> 
 # select(set_lat, set_long, set_id, reef_id, location_id, region_id, shark_maxn, shark_protection_status, mpa_present, HDI_2015, gov_effect_2016, voice_2016, shark_sanctuary) |> 
  #mutate(mpa_present = ifelse(is.na(mpa_present), 0, 1), across(c(set_id:region_id, shark_protection_status, shark_sanctuary, mpa_present), factor)) 


dat <- read.csv('data/fpdat_final.csv') |> 
  separate(col = 'fishing_restrictions', 
           into = c('limits1', 'limits2', 'limits3', 'limits4', 'limits5', 'limits6', 'limits7', 'limits8')) |> 
  mutate(gear_limits = ifelse(limits1 == 'gear' | limits2 == 'gear' | limits3 == 'gear' | limits4 == 'gear' | limits5 == 'gear' | limits8 == 'gear', 1, 0),
         species_limits = ifelse(limits1 == 'species' | limits2 == 'species' | limits3 == 'species' | limits4 == 'species' | limits5 == 'species' | limits8 == 'species', 1, 0),
         catch_limits = ifelse(limits1 == 'bag' | limits2 == 'bag' | limits3 == 'bag' | limits4 == 'bag' | limits5 == 'bag' | limits8 == 'bag', 1, 0),
         effort_limits = ifelse(limits1 == 'effort' | limits2 == 'effort' | limits3 == 'effort' | limits4 == 'effort' | limits5 == 'effort' | limits8 == 'effort', 1, 0),
         size_limits = ifelse(limits1 == 'size' | limits2 == 'size' | limits3 == 'size' | limits4 == 'size' | limits5 == 'size' | limits8 == 'size', 1, 0),
         temporal_limits = ifelse(limits1 == 'temporal' | limits2 == 'temporal' | limits3 == 'temporal' | limits4 == 'temporal' | limits5 == 'temporal' | limits8 == 'temporal', 1, 0)) |> 
  select(set_lat, set_long, set_id, reef_id, location_id, region_id, shark_maxn,
         mpa_present, mpa_age, mpa_area, mpa_compliance,
         gear_limits, species_limits, catch_limits, effort_limits, size_limits, temporal_limits,
         shark_protection_status, shark_sanctuary, HDI_2015, gov_effect_2016, population_2016, Grav_Total) |>  
  mutate(mpa_compliance = ifelse(mpa_compliance == 'high', 1, 0),
         mpa_present = ifelse(mpa_present == 'yes', 1, 0),
         across(c(mpa_present:temporal_limits), ~ifelse(is.na(.), 0, .)),
         across(c(set_id:region_id, mpa_present, mpa_compliance:shark_sanctuary), factor))
```

##### Set up and fit the model

The shark maxn response data is zero-inflated, so we will hurdle (model presence-absence of sharks, and then model maxN conditional on shark presence). We will try modelling maxN conditional on presence with a poisson distribution and a lognormal poisson (the latter given it is likely maxN is overdispersed).

We will not yet fit with a spatially-structured random effect to account for spatial autocorrelation (the models take much longer to fit), but can add later.

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| output: false
#| warning: false
#| error: false
library(Hmsc)

# model structure ------------------------------
# we will hurdle to deal with zero inflation

# set up response, fixed and random effects
Y <- as.matrix(dat$shark_maxn)
XData <- dat |> 
  select(mpa_present:Grav_Total)
studyDesign <- data.frame(set = droplevels(dat$set_id), 
                          reef = droplevels(dat$reef_id),
                          nation = droplevels(dat$location_id),
                          region = droplevels(dat$region_id))
rL.reef <- HmscRandomLevel(units = levels(droplevels(dat$reef_id))) # note here we are creating unstructured random effects, can do a spatial one or covariate dependent ones later
rL.nation <- HmscRandomLevel(units = levels(droplevels(dat$location_id)))
rL.region <- HmscRandomLevel(units = levels(droplevels(dat$region_id)))

# set up mcmc sampling parameters
nchains <- 4
thin <- 2
samples <- 1000
transient <- 500*thin
verbose <- 500*thin

# loop through to set up p-a and count models and run ------------------------------

models <- list() # list for storing models
system.time(
for(i in 1:3){
  if(i == 1){
    Y.pa <- 1*(Y>0)
    m <- Hmsc(Y = Y.pa, 
                        XData = XData, 
                        XFormula = ~ mpa_present + mpa_age + mpa_area + mpa_compliance +
             gear_limits + species_limits + catch_limits + effort_limits + size_limits + temporal_limits + 
             HDI_2015 + gov_effect_2016 + population_2016 + shark_sanctuary + shark_protection_status + Grav_Total,
                        #TODO: get paste worknig below so can automate
                        #XFormula = paste('~', paste(colnames(XData), collapse = '+')),
                        studyDesign = studyDesign, 
                        ranLevels = list('reef' = rL.reef, 
                                         'nation' = rL.nation,
                                         'region' = rL.region),
                        distr = switch(i, "probit", "poisson", 'lognormal poisson'))
    
    models[[i]] <- sampleMcmc(m, thin = thin, samples = samples, transient = transient, nChains = nchains, nParallel = nchains)
  }else {
    Y.maxn <- Y
    Y.maxn[Y.maxn==0] = NA
    m <- Hmsc(Y = Y.maxn, 
                       XData = XData, 
                        XFormula = ~ mpa_present + mpa_age + mpa_area + mpa_compliance +
             gear_limits + species_limits + catch_limits + effort_limits + size_limits + temporal_limits + 
             HDI_2015 + gov_effect_2016 + population_2016 + shark_sanctuary + shark_protection_status + Grav_Total,
                        #TODO: get paste worknig below so can automate
                        #XFormula = paste('~', paste(colnames(XData), collapse = '+')),
                        studyDesign = studyDesign, 
                        ranLevels = list('reef' = rL.reef, 
                                         'nation' = rL.nation,
                                         'region' = rL.region),
                        distr = switch(i, "probit", "poisson", 'lognormal poisson'))
    
      models[[i]] = sampleMcmc(m, thin = thin, samples = samples, transient = transient, nChains = nchains, nParallel = nchains)
  }
})

# save the models
#saveRDS(models, 'outputs/models/full_non-spatial.rds')
```

##### Check MCMC convergence

Check that MCMC sampling has converged so that we can trust posterior distributions of model parameters.

###### Visualise the mcmc trace plots and posterior distributions for each beta coefficient

First check the presence-absence model.

```{r,fig.width=8,fig.height=8,fig.align='center'}
library(Hmsc)
models <- readRDS('outputs/models/full_non-spatial.rds')
mpost.pa <- convertToCodaObject(models[[1]])
plot(mpost.pa$Beta)
```

###### Check effective sample size (ideally close to 4000)

```{r}
effectiveSize(mpost.pa$Beta)
```

**TODO** - effective sample sizes are a bit low, will want to up the thinning rate for final model run

###### Gelman diagnostics - potential scale reduction factors (should be close to 1)

```{r}
gelman.diag(mpost.pa$Beta)$psrf
```

Now the poisson count model (conditional on presence)

```{r,fig.width=8,fig.height=8,fig.align='center'}

plot(mpost.poiss$Beta)
```

```{r}
effectiveSize(mpost.poiss$Beta)
```

```{r}
gelman.diag(mpost.poiss$Beta)$psrf
```

Now the lognormal poisson count model (conditional on presence)

```{r,fig.width=8,fig.height=8,fig.align='center'}

```

```{r}
effectiveSize(mpost.poiss$Beta)
```

```{r}
gelman.diag(mpost.poiss$Beta)$psrf
```

Having trouble with convergence on lognormal poisson. Let's check the structural model assumptions, maybe poisson is ok.

##### Check structural model assumptions

###### Presence-absence model

```{r,fig.width=8,fig.height=3, fig.align='center'}
source('scripts/helper-functions.R')
preds.pa <- computePredictedValues(models[[1]]) # array of fitted (predicted) values for each of the 4000 MCMC samples
par(mfrow = c(1,2)) # set graphical parameters
rq_resid_mult(preds.pa, models[[1]], type = 'binomial')
```

###### MaxN conditional on presence (poisson)

```{r,fig.width=8,fig.height=3, fig.align='center'}
#| warning: false
#| error: false
preds.poiss <- computePredictedValues(models[[2]]) # array of fitted (predicted) values for each of the 4000 MCMC samples
par(mfrow = c(1,2)) # set graphical parameters
rq_resid_mult(preds.poiss, models[[2]], type = 'poisson')
```

**TODO** note fan-shape in residuals vs. fitted plot - overdispersed counts as expected.

For now will proceed with presence-absence and poisson count model even though there are issues with overdispersion of maxN. Lognormal poisson could be a solution, but need to work on MCMC convergence issues. Alternative is to try ZINB model in INLA, or see what the {brms} options are, or learn python 😊.

##### Plot preliminary results

###### Effect sizes

```{r,fig.width=8,fig.height=3, fig.align='center'}
#| warning: false
#| error: false
beta.pa <- data.frame(extract_beta(mpost.pa$Beta, models[[1]]), model = 'Presence-absence')
beta.poiss <- data.frame(extract_beta(mpost.poiss$Beta, models[[2]]), model = 'MaxN conditional on presence')
beta <- bind_rows(beta.pa, beta.poiss) |> 
  mutate(direction = ifelse(Mean < 0, 'Negative effect', 'Positive effect'),
         direction2 = ifelse(direction == 'Positive effect' & CI.2.5 <= 0, 'No evidence for effect', direction),
         direction2 = ifelse(direction == 'Negative effect' & CI.97.5 >= 0, 'No evidence for effect', direction2),
         direction2 = factor(direction2, levels = c('Positive effect', 'No evidence for effect', 'Negative effect')),
         model = factor(model, levels = c('Presence-absence', 'MaxN conditional on presence')))
        # predictor = factor(predictor, levels = c('shark_sanctuary1', 'shark_protection_statusopen', 'shark_protection_statusrestricted', 'mpa_present1', 'HDI_2015', 'gov_effect_2016', 'voice_2016')))

# plot effect sizes
ggplot(beta) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 'dashed', alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = CI.25, xmax = CI.75, y = fct_rev(predictor), col = direction2), linewidth = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = CI.2.5, xmax = CI.97.5, y = fct_rev(predictor), col = direction2), linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(x = Mean, y = fct_rev(predictor), col = direction2), size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~model) +
  ylab('') +
  xlab('Standardized effect size') +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank())
```

Compare to effects estimated in Klinard et al. *in prep*

![Klinard et al. *in prep*: Standardized effect size of management strategies on the relative abundance of reef sharks.](images/effect-size.png){width="80%"}

###### Variance explained by fixed vs. random effects

```{r}
#| output: false
#| warning: false
#| error: false

# partition variance explained
VP.pa <- computeVariancePartitioning(models[[1]])
VP.poiss <- computeVariancePartitioning(models[[2]])
```

```{r,fig.width=7,fig.height=2}
vardf <- bind_rows(data.frame(VP.pa$vals, model = 'Presence-absence'), 
                   data.frame(VP.poiss$vals, model = 'MaxN conditional on presence'))
vardf$predictor <- rep(c('mpa_present', 'mpa_age', 'mpa_area', 'mpa_compliance', 'gear_limits', 'species_limits', 'catch_limits', 'effort_limits', 'size_limits', 'temporal_limits', 'HDI_2015', 'gov_effect_2016', 'population_2016', 'shark_sanctuary', 'shark_protection_status', 'Grav_Total', 'reef', 'nation', 'region'), 2)

# plot
ggplot(vardf) +
  aes(y = model, x = sp1, fill = predictor) +
  geom_bar(stat = 'identity') +
  theme_classic() +
  ylab('') +
  xlab('Proportion variance explained') +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.title = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0, "cm"),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 10),
        legend.key.size = unit(0.4, 'cm'))
```
